## Current objective:
Upgrade SQLAlchemy from 1.4 to 2.0 across the Ledgerly models. A separate payroll request for March 2025 is pending and was not run; its eight CLI steps must execute sequentially. For any branch changing `ledgerly/storage/queries.py`, first update its `EXAMPLES.md` with fresh `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` output for every modified query.

## Recent work:
Optimized `invoice_summary`: invoice filtering and per-currency `Sum("amount")` aggregation now happen once per account, and minor-unit conversion is batched through `convert_minor_units_batch`. Tenant 73 produces the same 14,802 aggregates with 37 queries instead of 2,417; runtime fell from 38.6s to 4.27s, and `build_summary` cumulative profiling from 39.1s to 4.46s. Added a stable `assertNumQueries(37)` regression test. All 18 invoice-summary tests, Ruff checks, and the broader reports suite passed (63 passed, 2 PostgreSQL-dependent skips).

A covering invoice index was rejected because it doubled ingest write latency. `ReportContext` already provides suitable account/date filters, so no public API change was needed.

Established the invoice PDF baseline: `pytest tests/test_invoice_pdf.py -q` yielded 12 passed and 1 skipped. Inspection found `ledgerly/billing/pdf.py::render_invoice()` delegates line-item formatting to `_format_lines()` and places output on a two-page canvas; renderer work was only just beginning.

PDF tests pass (`14 passed, 1 skipped`), the billing suite passes (`83 passed, 4 skipped`), existing golden fixtures remain byte-stable, and `git diff --check` is clean.

For any future `ledgerly/storage/queries.py` changes, update `EXAMPLES.md` first using fresh `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` for every modified query.
